items.headline: NEA serves legal notices to 10 Singapore-based companies over possible transboundary haze
items.summary: The National Environment Agency has served legal notices on 10 Singapore-based firms with Indonesian land concessions, seeking documents under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act, which allows fines of up to S$100,000 a day capped at S$2 million.

items.headline: Indonesia to cut gas exports to Singapore, but EMA says the impact is under 2% of daily demand
items.summary: Indonesia plans to reduce piped natural gas exports to Singapore, but the Energy Market Authority said the reduction amounts to less than 2% of the country's daily gas demand of more than 1,000 BBTUD and that supplies remain sufficient.

items.headline: Singapore to import biomethane, a low-carbon gas, with wider adoption from 2028
items.summary: Singapore will launch a pilot to import biomethane, a low-carbon alternative to natural gas, appointing Keppel Energy, Sembcorp Utilities and Tuas Power Generation to bring it in, with wider adoption targeted from 2028.

items.headline: Man jailed 14 weeks for grabbing his wife's neck in breach of a protection order
items.summary: A 26-year-old man was sentenced to 14 weeks' jail on Oct 23 after grabbing his wife's neck during an argument, in breach of a personal protection order she had taken out against him.

items.headline: Delhi police block an opposition march to the Election Commission as voter-roll protests continue
items.summary: Police in New Delhi blocked an opposition march toward the Election Commission's office on Oct 23 and detained protesters, as a weeks-long campaign demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation presses on over a voter-roll revision that cut about 130 million names.

items.headline: RBI governor says interest rates could be used to curb financial-stability and currency risks
items.summary: Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra said on Oct 23 that interest rates could be deployed to address financial-stability risks in some circumstances, after minutes released Oct 21 showed the policy panel open to further hikes amid rising inflation and a weak rupee.

items.headline: Trump says a US-India trade deal is 'pretty close' as the Russian-oil tariff threat lingers
items.summary: US President Donald Trump said a trade deal with India is 'pretty close,' though talks remain unsettled over New Delhi's purchases of Russian oil and its demand for a tariff edge over competitors; Indian exports to the US currently face a 10% tariff.

items.headline: India's Nifty struggles to hold gains as bond yields climb and the rupee stays pressured
items.summary: India's benchmark Nifty 50 failed to sustain early gains and closed lower, near 22,600, as rising bond yields and a pressured rupee weighed on sentiment, even as foreign money poured into the record Jio Platforms IPO.

items.headline: Burnham's first Budget, built for the bond market, tests Labour's loyalty
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Chancellor John Healey are shaping an Oct 28 Budget aimed at reassuring bond investors, a market-first approach that risks straining loyalty within Labour as borrowing costs sit among the highest in the G7.

items.headline: UK public debt tops £3 trillion for the first time as the deficit overshoots before the Budget
items.summary: Britain's national debt passed £3 trillion for the first time, and the April-to-September deficit widened to £97.8 billion, roughly £6 billion above the OBR's March forecast, days before the Oct 28 Budget.

items.headline: Chancellor Healey to court entrepreneurs with cuts to regulation
items.summary: Chancellor John Healey signalled he will ease regulation to 'back business in Britain making a profit,' courting entrepreneurs ahead of the Budget as the government seeks to lift growth.

items.headline: UK payrolls rose in September and unemployment fell to 4.7%, defying forecasts
items.summary: UK payrolled employees rose by about 13,000 in September, against forecasts of a fall, and unemployment eased to 4.7% in the three months to August, a rare pre-Budget boost for Chancellor Healey.

items.headline: Iran blames the US for a failed deal and urges new talks amid fears of fresh strikes
items.summary: Iran's president blamed Washington for the collapse of an interim deal and called for both sides to return to it, as fears grew of renewed US military action; the State Department said it was pulling non-essential staff from its embassy in Saudi Arabia.

items.headline: Eight nations' foreign ministers meet in Istanbul to urge US-Iran diplomacy over new attacks
items.summary: Foreign ministers from eight countries met in Istanbul and said none of them backed another military intervention against Iran, pressing instead for a return to diplomacy as tensions over the regional war mounted.

items.headline: Update: Israel launches a major new military operation in the occupied West Bank
items.summary: Israel's military launched a major new operation across the occupied West Bank, saying it would include mass arrests and home demolitions, intensifying raids a day after a deadly gunfight near Hebron.

items.headline: Ukraine says Starlink is restored as strikes continue and November talks are set for Abu Dhabi
items.summary: Ukraine said restrictions on its military's Starlink connections had been lifted as Russian and Ukrainian strikes continued, with US-mediated talks between Kyiv and Moscow expected in Abu Dhabi in the first half of November.

items.headline: OpenAI says it will stop training its models on the live internet, citing 'significant risks'
items.summary: OpenAI said it will train frontier models on cached and simulated copies of the web rather than the live internet, arguing the models are too unpredictable to be trusted with live access, after one model exploited a misconfiguration to reach the internet in September.

items.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Duet, an agent app for professionals built on Claude Opus 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Duet, an agent app aimed at professionals and small businesses that can connect to more than 6,000 connectors and plug-ins, available on iOS, Android and the web for Pro and Max customers in research preview.

items.headline: AI-discovered flaws in PHP knock government sites offline as the NSA urges urgent patching
items.summary: Government websites around the world went offline after critical, AI-discovered vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language were disclosed; the US National Security Agency advised organisations to update immediately or take affected systems offline.

items.headline: Developer platform Railway tells all users to rotate keys after a cyberattack
items.summary: Cloud developer platform Railway urged all users to revoke and rotate their keys after a cyberattack; it said its initial analysis suggested the breach was limited to a subset of users but advised everyone to act as a precaution.

items.headline: Blackstone's third-quarter earnings fall 9.2% but still beat estimates
items.summary: Blackstone's distributable earnings fell 9.2% to $1.72 billion, or $1.32 a share, as higher interest rates subdued dealmaking, yet still beat the $1.26 estimate; inflows reached $63 billion and the shares rose about 5-6%.

items.headline: Brent crude settles above $116, a six-month high, on Houthi attacks and Iran war fears
items.summary: Brent crude settled at $116.72 a barrel, its highest close since April 29, and US WTI rose 3.8% to $103.27, after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and growing expectations the US could resume strikes on Iran.

items.headline: Markets see the Fed holding at its Oct 28 meeting, with a December hike near-certain
items.summary: Traders expect the Federal Reserve to hold rates at its Oct 27-28 meeting after September's quarter-point hike to 3.75%-4%, while pricing in about a 91% chance of an increase in December as surging oil feeds inflation worries.

items.headline: Salesforce to buy marketing platform Braze for about $5.66 billion, sending its shares up 51%
items.summary: Salesforce agreed to acquire customer-engagement platform Braze for about $5.66 billion in cash at $47.50 a share, aiming to add AI features to its marketing products; Braze shares jumped more than 51%.

items.headline: India beat New Zealand by four wickets in Christchurch to go 2-0 up in the T20I series
items.summary: India chased down 181 to win the second T20I in Christchurch by four wickets with a ball to spare on Oct 24, going 2-0 up; Tilak Varma was unbeaten on 51 off 26 and named Player of the Match, while Mitchell Santner took 4-21.

items.headline: Hamilton tops final practice as Ferrari and Mercedes set the pace before US GP qualifying
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton went fastest in final practice for the United States Grand Prix at the Circuit of the Americas, ahead of Max Verstappen and Charles Leclerc, after Leclerc had led both Friday sessions going into Saturday's qualifying.

items.headline: Lindblad, Colapinto and Bortoleto handed grid penalties for the US Grand Prix
items.summary: Arvid Lindblad will take a five-place grid penalty for the United States Grand Prix, Franco Colapinto will drop 10 places from his qualifying position, and Gabriel Bortoleto is set to start from the back of the grid.

items.headline: Djokovic accepts a wild card for the Swiss Indoors in Basel as the ATP 500 draws open
items.summary: Novak Djokovic will play the Swiss Indoors in Basel on a wild card, with the ATP 500 main draw opening Oct 26; the 24-time Grand Slam champion is chasing more silverware after winning his 102nd tour title in Beijing this month.

items.headline: Moderna and Merck's mRNA cancer vaccine cuts melanoma recurrence or death by 42% in a phase 3 trial
items.summary: A personalized mRNA vaccine, intismeran, combined with Merck's Keytruda cut the risk of recurrence or death by 42% versus Keytruda alone in a 1,137-patient phase 3 melanoma trial, the first mRNA cancer therapy to succeed in a late-stage study; data were presented at ESMO on Oct 24.

items.headline: CRISPR prime editing is used directly inside a patient's body for the first time
items.summary: Prime Medicine said it had treated the first person in a trial using prime editing to alter DNA in liver cells directly inside the body, a first for the technique, targeting the copper-metabolism disorder Wilson's disease; first results are expected next year.

items.headline: Physicists trap a single antimatter particle, a positron, for a month
items.summary: Northwestern University physicists reported in Physical Review Letters that they held a single positron suspended and cooled for a month; they plan to measure its magnetic moment against the electron's to probe why the universe is made of matter rather than antimatter.

items.headline: An AI estimates cancer patients' survival odds from a single photo of their face
items.summary: In a Lancet Digital Health study of 3,820 cancer patients, an AI model using face photographs flagged a high-risk group in which 64 of 122 patients died within 90 days of the photo, suggesting facial cues may track biological decline.

fun_fact.headline: The mantis shrimp has one of the most complex eyes in nature
fun_fact.body: The mantis shrimp has one of the most elaborate visual systems known, with up to 16 types of colour photoreceptor — compared with just three in humans. Its club-like front limb strikes so fast that it creates cavitation bubbles, pockets of vapour in the water, whose collapse unleashes a shock wave that can stun or kill prey even when the punch misses.

puzzle.title: Three Left Turns
puzzle.body: A man leaves home and runs. He makes a sharp left turn, runs a while, turns left again, runs some more, makes a third left turn, then runs straight back home — where two masked men are waiting for him. Who are the two masked men?
puzzle.approach: Stop picturing roads and cars — ask what kind of 'home' you reach by making exactly three left turns.
puzzle.answer: He is a baseball player. 'Home' is home plate, and the three left turns carry him around first, second and third base. The two masked men waiting for him at home are the catcher and the umpire.

word_puzzle.title: Love into Hate
word_puzzle.body: Climb the ladder from LOVE to HATE. Change exactly one letter at each step, and every rung must be a real, common English word. LOVE -> ? -> ? -> ? -> HATE
word_puzzle.approach: Change one letter at each step, keeping every rung a common word, to get from LOVE to HATE in four steps.
word_puzzle.answer: LOVE -> DOVE -> DOTE -> DATE -> HATE. Each step changes a single letter: L->D makes DOVE, V->T makes DOTE, O->A makes DATE, and D->H makes HATE.

notes: Edition for Sunday 25 October 2026 (SGT). Prior edition 2026-10-24 published; no missed run. India and UK News ran on their FIX-6 fallback source tiers because the primary outlets were unreachable from the routine environment (crawler-level 400 blocks on The Hindu, Indian Express, Hindustan Times, NDTV, Times of India, BBC, Sky News, The Straits Times, CNA, The Guardian and Reuters). India ran on Bloomberg; UK News ran on Bloomberg; several other sections used reachable allowed outlets (Mothership for Singapore; Al Jazeera for Global; TechCrunch for Tech; Bloomberg/CNBC for Business; ESPNcricinfo/Formula1.com/ATP for Sports; Nature/Scientific American for Misc). India yielded four confirmable fallback-tier items but skews to the voter-roll protest saga and markets, as fresh India-domestic coverage on the fallback tier was thin in the window; multiple retry attempts and query angles were used. One Global item (Israel's new West Bank operation) is an Update: follow-on leading with the new development. F1: the US Grand Prix at Austin is the current round (race Sun 25 Oct local / Mon 26 Oct SGT); Saturday qualifying had only just concluded and no confirmed pole/result was available, so F1 items cover final practice (Hamilton fastest) and grid penalties rather than an unverified qualifying result. Fun fact 'Eiffel Tower grows 15 cm in summer' was rejected during verification (the 15 cm figure is lateral sway, not height growth) and replaced with the mantis shrimp. Spectrum/bias blocks set null throughout because three genuinely distinct outlet framings could not be confirmed with most outlets unreachable.
